# Writing a `ui-surface` page

Generated from `ui-surface`'s own template declarations. It states what this type requires;
the rules that apply to every page are in `wiki-authoring-spec.md` beside this file.

- **Lives at** `design/surfaces/<module>/<feature-slug>.md` — one page per feature, structured by named surface
- **Authorship** `curated` — an agent may draft it; a human approves
- **Freshness** stale after 90d
- **Template version** 2 — set `template-version: 2`

## Frontmatter

Required on this type beyond the base fields (`title`, `type`, `created`, `updated`, `owner`, `authorship`):

- `feature`
- `flows`
- `platforms`

The template also scaffolds `template-version`, `sources`, `related`, `invalidates`, `origination`, `confidence` — fill or empty each one; leaving a placeholder is an error.

`owner:` is fixed to `design` — do not change it.

## Placeholders to replace

{{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}}. Leaving one in place is an error (`unsubstituted-token`), and so is leaving a template example line (`template-example-line`).

The body also carries 23 placeholders written in angle brackets — `<Surface name>`, `<always / role / state>`, `<destination, or —>`, `<entity field / derived from … / input / static / external: … / system: … / Pending: …>`, `<entity>`, `<event>`, `<flow-slug>`, `<helper / placeholder / tooltip: text>`, `<kind>`, `<label>`, `<module>`, `<primary / secondary / destructive / nav / view>`, `<required / optional>`, `<rule → message; when checked>`, `<state>`, `<text / currency / date / badge…>`, `<text input / select / date picker…>`, `<the call>`, `<value / —>`, `<what happens>`, `<what is unresolved>`, `<what the user sees change>`, `<when enabled>`. Each stands for content you write; replace every one, including in a row whose other cells you have already filled. Leaving one is an error (`unsubstituted-placeholder`).

## Where this type may link

This page lives in `design/` (layer 2).

You may link to `domain/`, `product/` — and to other pages in `design/`.

You may not link to `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`. Those sub-wikis cite this one, never the other way round; when you need to name something there, name it in prose instead of linking it.

## After you save

Two steps finish the page and neither is in the template:

- Commit the file under your own identity — authorship is a git fact, not a frontmatter one.
- Run `/wiki-reindex` so the page appears in its sub-wiki `index.md` and in `_derived/cited-by.md`. Until then it exists but nothing links to it.
